subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should this issue be resolved by splitting the restart catch-up fix from a separate emergency outbound-stop/delete-abort design, or should one combined core change own both behaviors?
rationale: Current code proof shows a real replay bug and a partial cancellation mitigation, but the requested emergency stop changes product and owner boundaries across cron, gateway lifecycle, task cancellation, and channel delivery.

options.title: Split Replay Fix And Emergency Design
options.body: Land or replace the activation-boundary PR for stale restart replay, then design the user-facing emergency stop/delete behavior as a separate core/gateway decision.

options.title: Combine Into One Core Fix
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella for a single broader change that covers restart replay, cron remove aborts, gateway stop behavior, and outbound delivery blocking.

options.title: Scope To Replay Only
options.body: Close the stop/delete/emergency portion as a separate product request and treat only stale cron catch-up as the remaining bug.

recommendation.title: Split Replay Fix And Emergency Design
recommendation.body: Land or replace the activation-boundary PR for stale restart replay, then design the user-facing emergency stop/delete behavior as a separate core/gateway decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron path history and land-ready verification on the candidate PR make this the best available routing owner for the product boundary choice.
